original_question: Is it possible to devise a computer program that runs on a modern computer in real time, enumerates all natural solutions of the geodetic system of Diophantine equations associated with the Hoffman-Singleton graph, and thereby generates and determines the general number of all geodetic graphs of diameter d >= 2 that are homeomorphic to the Hoffman-Singleton graph?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the paper’s official statement in “B. Open Problems Related to Construction and Enumeration,” specifically open problem 2: whether one can devise a computer program, to run on a modern computer in real time, that enumerates all natural solutions of the geodetic system of Diophantine equations associated with the Hoffman-Singleton graph and thereby generates and finds the general number of all geodetic graphs of diameter d ≥ 2 homeomorphic to it, as was done for the Petersen graph in [6]. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target almost verbatim: it asks for a computer program, mentions real-time execution on a modern computer, focuses on enumerating all natural solutions of the geodetic Diophantine system associated with the Hoffman-Singleton graph, and connects that enumeration to generating and counting all geodetic graphs of diameter at least 2 that are homeomorphic to the Hoffman-Singleton graph. Those are exactly the central ingredients of open problem 2 in Section B. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
missing_details: The paper poses this question only after the standing assumption that the preceding characterization conjectures are true; in nearby context, those conjectures assert that for graphs homeomorphic to Moore graphs, the three listed conditions are not merely sufficient but necessary as well. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

A stand-alone version should define the graph-theoretic terms used implicitly: a geodetic graph has a unique geodesic between every two distinct vertices; a segment is a path whose only nodes are its endpoints; and two graphs are homeomorphic if both can be obtained by inserting vertices on edges. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

The base graph should be identified more explicitly: the Hoffman-Singleton graph is treated here as a Moore graph/geodetic block of diameter 2 and degree 7. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

Your draft uses d both as the diameter threshold in the target class and, implicitly, as if it were the base graph’s diameter. To avoid ambiguity, a stand-alone formulation should separate the fixed diameter 2 of the Hoffman-Singleton graph from the variable diameter D ≥ 2 of the graphs being generated, matching the notation used in the earlier algorithmic paper. ([mililink.com](https://www.mililink.com/upload/article/107744499ijgta_v3i1_13-44.pdf))

The phrase “geodetic system of Diophantine equations associated with the Hoffman-Singleton graph” is not self-explanatory by itself. In the cited earlier paper, the analogous construction for a fixed geodetic graph uses a fundamental basis of odd circuits together with all even circuits of lengths 4,6,…,2d+2; for the Hoffman-Singleton case the authors report 126 odd 5-cycles and 5250 even 6-cycles, yielding a system of 5376 linear Diophantine equations in 175 unknowns. ([mililink.com](https://www.mililink.com/upload/article/107744499ijgta_v3i1_13-44.pdf))

“Natural solutions” should be made explicit as solutions in natural numbers for the segment-length variables of that linear Diophantine system. This paper is not an algebra-over-a-field problem: there are no ambient field/ring choices, homogeneity conditions, degree restrictions, or nilpotency hypotheses to specify beyond the natural-number domain of the unknowns. ([mililink.com](https://www.mililink.com/upload/article/107744499ijgta_v3i1_13-44.pdf))

The term “general number” is paper-specific and should be clarified. In [6], it means the total count of all such homeomorphic geodetic graphs in the author’s counting convention, not merely the number up to isomorphism. ([mililink.com](https://www.mililink.com/upload/article/107744499ijgta_v3i1_13-44.pdf))

The phrase “in real time on a modern computer” is part of the paper’s wording, but it is informal and receives no formal complexity-theoretic definition. A sharper research question should either mark that phrase as informal or replace it with “effective/explicit computer program.” ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
refined_question: Assuming the paper’s preceding characterization conjecture for graphs homeomorphic to Moore graphs—namely, that a graph G homeomorphic to a Moore graph of diameter d is geodetic exactly when (i) every path of d successive segments is a geodesic, (ii) every cycle with 2d+1 segments has odd length, and (iii) all cycles with 2d+2 segments have the same length—can one devise an explicit computer program (the paper informally says “to be run in a modern computer in real time”) which, for the Hoffman-Singleton graph H (the Moore graph of degree 7 and diameter 2), constructs and solves the associated geodetic system of linear Diophantine equations, enumerates all of its natural-number solutions, and thereby, for each integer D ≥ 2, generates every geodetic graph of diameter D homeomorphic to H and determines the paper’s “general number” of such graphs, i.e. the total count rather than only the count up to isomorphism? ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s actual intent, because it reproduces the wording and scope of Section B, open problem 2 almost exactly. I did not broaden it beyond that problem. The main refinements needed to make it stand alone are: (a) making explicit the conjectural assumption under which the construction/enumeration program is posed, (b) defining geodetic, segment, homeomorphic, and the role of the Hoffman-Singleton graph as a Moore graph of diameter 2, (c) distinguishing the fixed base diameter 2 from the variable diameter D of the generated graphs, and (d) clarifying the paper-specific counting phrase “general number” by using the meaning supplied in [6]. The earlier paper [6] also supplies the concrete computational context for the Hoffman-Singleton case—5376 equations in 175 unknowns—which explains why the 2022 note phrases this as a programming/enumeration challenge rather than as a purely abstract existence question. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
